result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.prize_collecting_steiner_tree()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Find a prize-collecting Steiner tree. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L28084-L28173){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.prize_collecting_steiner_tree( prizes, edge_penalty=1.0, weight_attr=None, return_subgraph=True, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} A variant of the Steiner tree where each node has a *prize* (benefit of inclusion) and each edge has a *cost* (penalty for inclusion). The algorithm finds a connected subtree that maximizes total prize minus total edge cost. Unlike the standard Steiner tree, not all prize nodes need to be included if the cost of connecting them is too high. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [prizes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict[str, float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Dictionary mapping node labels to prize values (e.g., `-log10(p_value)` from GWAS hits). Only nodes with prizes are candidates for inclusion. [edge_penalty]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Multiplier applied to edge weights as costs. Higher values penalize longer paths more aggressively, producing smaller trees. Default `1.0`. [weight_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Edge attribute to use for weights. If `None`, uses the edge's weight field. [return_subgraph]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), returns a new Graph. If `False`, returns edge tuples. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph or list[tuple[str, str, float]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The prize-collecting Steiner tree as a graph or edge list. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If any prize node doesn't exist in the graph. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#68fc4f9d .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(weighted=True) .add_node(label="BRCA1") .add_node(label="TP53") .add_node(label="ATM") .add_node(label="CHEK2") .add_node(label="MDM2") .add_edge("BRCA1", "ATM", weight=1.0) .add_edge("ATM", "CHEK2", weight=1.0) .add_edge("TP53", "MDM2", weight=1.0) .add_edge("ATM", "TP53", weight=2.0) ) tree = graph.prize_collecting_steiner_tree( prizes={"BRCA1": 5.0, "TP53": 3.0, "CHEK2": 4.0} ) tree.count_nodes(), tree.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (4, 3) ``` ::: :::
